en: The Sūtra on the Six-Syllable King of Mantras, translated by an unknown person and now appended to the catalogue of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Buddha was staying in the Jeta Grove in the kingdom of Śrāvastī. At that time...

There was a Caṇḍāla woman of a non-Buddhist sect who sought to bewitch and delude the Venerable Ānanda; at that moment, the Tathāgata perceived Ānanda’s confusion and spoke for him the Sūtra of the Six-Syllable King of Mantras.
What was spoken by previous Buddhas, I now speak as well.
He then spoke the mantra:

Andhare | Pandare | Karaje | Kiyule | Tiṣyavati | Bindhavati | Dhatule | Dhavale | Dhakumavati | Sumavati | Andarapandarale | Dandare | Tidure | Anantamanavati | Anānaya | Mathumavatikarata | Kiyule | Bodhigamati | Tisyavati | Bindhumati | Arava | Gavati-vitha-vithani | Cittha-vithani | Svāhā. If anyone should cast an evil spell or curse against such-and-such a person...
Whether already made or yet to be made,
whether by devas, nāgas, yakṣas, or rākṣasas.
Whether they be hungry ghosts (preta),
kumbhāṇḍas, pūtanas, piśācas, apasmāras, or kiṃkaras.
Whether it be a Kahoḍa, a Vaitāla, a Vaitālika, a female Vaitālika, a śramaṇa, or a brāhmaṇa.
Whether they be kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, śūdras, mātaṅgas, or mātaṅga women.
Whether they be caṇḍālas or caṇḍāla women,
whether slaves or maidservants,
whether men or women.
If there are male or female practitioners who have left the household life among the non-Buddhists, and such various others who are all capable of performing curses,
incantations, and sorcery— I now [employ] this six-syllable King of Mantras Sūtra.
If one acts upward, one extinguishes it by acting upward;
if one acts downward, one extinguishes it by acting downward;
if one acts upon the ground, one extinguishes it by acting upon the ground.
If one acts upon a wall, it is extinguished upon the wall;
if one acts at the edge of a pillar, it is extinguished at the edge of the pillar;
if one acts within a city, it is extinguished within the city.
If it was committed within the city gate, it shall be extinguished within the city gate;
if it was committed within the palace, it shall be extinguished within the palace;
if it was committed within the palace gate, it shall be extinguished within the palace gate.
If they act on the main road, they shall be extinguished thereon;
if they act on a crossroads, they shall be extinguished thereon;
if they act as brahmins, they shall all be extinguished.
If one acts in the water, one extinguishes it in the water;
if one acts on the bank of the water, one extinguishes it on the bank of the water;
if one acts on the riverbank, one extinguishes it on the riverbank.
If one commits it within the house, one extinguishes it within the house;
if one commits it by the side of a tree, one extinguishes it by the side of the tree;
if one commits it at the root of a tree, one extinguishes it at the root of the tree.
If one commits [an offense] amidst a fire, one shall extinguish it amidst a fire;
if one commits it in a brazier, one shall extinguish it in a brazier;
if one commits it near a well or a hearth, one shall extinguish it near a well or a hearth.
If one commits it near a mortar and pestle, it is extinguished there;
if one commits it near a grave, it is extinguished there;
if one commits it amidst bedding and mats, it is extinguished there.
If one performs [the rite] with clothing, coverings, or ornaments, they shall all be extinguished;
if performed at night, it is extinguished at night;
if performed during the day, it is extinguished during the day.
If one constantly recites it day and night, all [obstacles] will be extinguished.
This mantra can sever the path of Indra’s spells;
it can sever the path of Brahmā’s spells.
It can sever the paths of incantations of the four heavens,
and it can completely sever all paths of incantations, spells, and arts of malevolent ghosts.
If anyone should perform rites of suppression, sorcery, or cursing against a certain person;
And all poisons shall be utterly extinguished.
Whether it be caused by khaḍga-vidyā, piśāca,
or pūtana, all such [harm] shall be utterly extinguished.
All evils are completely exhausted, and all virtues fill their place.
May this mantra be ever auspicious.
By means of these words of truth.
May [so-and-so] be at peace by day and at peace by night, always at peace day and night, attaining a lifespan of a hundred years and seeing a hundred autumns.
Why is this? Because in the world, there is nothing superior to the Buddha.
Respected by humans and devas, and venerated by the multitude of ghosts;
should there be those who practice the path of evil spells—
whether they have already done so, are about to do so, or are in the midst of doing so.
Whether already accomplished or not yet accomplished, all shall be extinguished;
likewise, all poisons capable of harming people shall be entirely eliminated by this King of Six-Syllable Mantras.
Then he spoke the mantra, saying:
*kha-ti kha-ju kha-vi-ti gam-syu gam-syu ta-ti ba-ti*. If someone should cast an evil spell or curse against such-and-such a person...
Whether they have already done it, or are about to do it—
whether they be devas, nāgas, yakṣas, or rākṣasas.
Furthermore, all those who are capable of performing evil incantations and curses shall be entirely extinguished.
Whether it be by means of *khārodaka*, *vidhara*,
or *putana*, whatever they may do shall be entirely extinguished.
All evils are utterly exhausted, and all virtues fill their place.
May this mantra be ever auspicious.

By means of these true words and phrases, may [Name] be peaceful by day and peaceful by night, peaceful always throughout the day and night, attaining a lifespan of a hundred years and seeing a hundred autumns.
Why is this? Because among the supreme dharmas of the world, none surpass the Buddha-dharma.
Honored by humans and devas, and accepted by the various spirits, it is free from desire and attachment.
Then he spoke the mantra, saying:
Kha-ji, kha-ju, kha-vi-ji, gam-shu gam-shu, ta-ji, ba-ji. Why is this? Because the Saṃgha is the supreme field of merit in the world.
Revered by humans and devas, and protected by the various spirits, he then spoke this mantra:
*Kha-ji* *kha-ju* *kha-vi-ji* *ghan-sau ghan-sau* *ta-ji* *ba-ji* *xing-ti* *a-ni-ti* *a-zhou-ti*. If anyone should cast evil spells or curses against such-and-such a person...
If blended poisons are present, they shall all be extinguished.
Then he spoke this mantra:

Ma-hu-po | O-mo-ti | O-mo-to | Sī-da-ni | Kha-ou-to | Po-ti-sī-da-ni | Pin-t’ou-mo-ti | Chi-ti-chi-to | Po-ti-sī-da-ni | A-pien-chien-to-pien | Ho-ho-c’a-li | Ho-ho-na-mi | Ho-ho-fu-mo-ti | Ho-ho-fu-to-ni-k’iu-c’a | Ho-ho-ni-ho-to | Kha-ou-to | Ni-p’i-c’a | Kha-ou-to | I-ni-mi-ni | To-to-p’ie Sva-hā. If there be anyone who reads and upholds this Great King of Mantras in Six Characters, [the poisons shall be destroyed].
If it were possible for a withered tree to be restored to life through incantations so that it might sprout branches and leaves once more,
how much more so for a human being?
May such-and-such a person attain a lifespan of a hundred years and behold a hundred autumns.
What has been taught by all Buddhas and transmitted by Ānanda—
if anyone reads and recites it until they have mastered it,
they will all protect themselves, and no evil will adhere to their person.
If one recites this for another, they will be able to eliminate that person's afflictions.
The reciter must abstain from the five pungent vegetables and maintain a sincere and pure mind;
only then can this practice be performed. *Namo Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva Mahāsattva*.
Having paid homage to that Great Being, I shall then recite this divine mantra.
May this divine mantra be ever auspicious.
O Avalokiteśvara, may you illuminate my body; having beheld my body, may you look upon me with compassion.
Then he spoke the mantra, saying:

U-ha-ni | Su-ha-ni | A-da-ni ha-da-ja-vi-ni | Dambhi-ni | An-ta-le | Pan-ta-le | Si-bi-ti | Pan-ta-ra | Pa-si-ni | Sa-lu-thu-rate | Tha-ba-ra-dhu-rate | Tha-chit-dam | Ja-ba-ya | Dam-ha-ya | Su-ha-ya | Ni-ba-ra-ya | Ya-ba-mu-ra-ti | Na-mu-cha-ti | Lu-lu-chi-tha | Pan-ta-si | Lu-lu-lu | Lu-chi-tha | Pan-ta-si | Svāhā | Ho-ri-li-chi | Li-shu-li | Matang-ki | Chandali-rākṣasa-rākṣasa-rāja | Svāhā. This mantra protects against all calamities.
Pure, stainless, and liberated;
illuminating with light, it binds all thieves—
the thieves who plunder and delude all, and the thieves who guard the body against evil.
Tigers, wolves, lions, mad elephants, and jackals are all bound. May I, [Name],
together with my fellow practitioners and companions,
be safe and auspicious wherever we go by the power of all mantras.
Homage to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
May this mantra be most auspicious.
On the day one employs this mantra-method, it should be maintained.
Do not consume the five pungent herbs; bathe thoroughly and remain pure.
Do not engage in sexual intercourse, nor drink alcohol or eat meat.
Holding a white cotton thread with the hand, recite the mantra seven times, tying one knot for each repetition.
If one is involved in legal matters, or is subjected to verbal abuse,
or engages in quarrels and disputes,
or is cursed by incantations— all such evils can be extinguished.
Having finished the incantation, tie this thread to the person’s sash or head-strap; after the matter has been resolved, the master himself shall untie it.
Homage to all Buddhas of the three periods of time: past, future, and present.
Homage to Mañjuśrī, Samantabhadra, Maitreya, and all the great Bodhisattvas.
Taking refuge in such a multitude of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas,
one should then recite this Great Divine Dhāraṇī mantra.
Then he spoke the mantra,
saying: *ṭaṃ duma-te yaśavate*.
Vārṣa devate uṣyadevate uttarani.
Acchayavati anuśanti muṣyavarāvamudi.
Parāva-jitu-si-pa-ti-karaṇi-gati-paviyasa-śūra-vare-dhiti-anuti-saṃdha-pati-uttaraṇi.
Śatamukha śatapāra viśanta kāliśa.
Vasana-bhagati-kauśalya-sanni-anusanti.
Vīśanti jñāti ajñāti tvaṃ nāgati.
Atānāgatiyāva sātiyā khaṇḍava-rāje.
brahṇe mule mūlamūla brahṇe śani paraluḥ
Sūriyadeva-tejo-paraloka-suvimale.
Amale: This mantra dispels all darkness;
it is upheld by the Tathāgata, revered and loved by all devas, protected by the multitude of deities, and understood by Brahmā.
It is reverently upheld and protected by Śakra and the World-Protectors;
it is definitively realized and maintained by all the noble ones and sages;
it harmonizes all natures and liberates one from all fetters.
All devas and humans sever all afflictions, subdue all demonic adversaries,
overcome all non-Buddhists, and crush all rival doctrines.
Furthermore, they surpass all arrogant Dharma masters;
they do not abandon the great assembly, gladden those who study the Dharma,
protect the treasury of the Dharma, and benefit the Triple Gem.
Compassionately pitying all classes of sentient beings, the adornment of these manifold meanings brings such benefits.
This is called the Dharani of the Inexhaustible Treasury; it is a protection that can protect where no other protection exists.
If there are those who read and recite it,
they shall obtain thirty-three kinds of fearlessness and freedom from peril.
Using this dhāraṇī method, one should rise at dawn, wash the hands, and rinse the mouth.
Burn incense and perform prostrations three times.
In whatever place you recite or engage in conversation,
in all such situations, one is impermanent and cannot surpass others.
Those who see it with reverence will rejoice, and enemies will be subdued;
such are its benefits. From the *Sūtra of the Six-Syllable King of Mantras* spoken by the Buddha.
